recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Memory, Mind, and the Human Biofield", "body": "Chance defined biofield tuning as the centropic process of bringing lost life force back into the body. He described the human biofield as a plasma around the body that holds the record of life experience, and said that neuroscience had never found memory stored in the brain, citing maze experiments on rats. From that, Chance concluded that the body was in the mind rather than the mind in the body. He said frozen or stuck fragments of the field limited the energy a person could reach, and that he held all injury and disease to be psychosomatic."}, {"title": "Cognitive Dissonance and Bodily Pain", "body": "The host asked about cognitive dissonance, and Chance said that in his experience it was the chief cause, if not the only cause, of pain and distortion in the body. He described it as holding two beliefs that were directly at odds yet fully believed. Chance said that recurring or chronic issues often turned out to involve such a clash, and that beliefs and expectations returned to people as repeating patterns in life. He added that these patterns were hard to see because they sat too close, like a nose, and that he was finding this kind of clash more often as his pattern recognition improved."}, {"title": "Simple Tools for Raising Your Energy", "body": "Chance recommended a weighted tuning fork, which he called the sonic slider, applied to the matching reflexology spot on the foot, and said he had used it for chest constriction and head and sinus discomfort. The host raised earthing, and Chance agreed that grounding mattered, since he saw the body as an electrical system. He also listed rest, deep breathing, fresh whole foods, spring water, and consciously receiving love and appreciation. He urged listeners to ask whether an activity or person felt like a drain or a gain, and to favor the gains."}, {"title": "Chance and John Question Official Narratives", "body": "Early in the talk Chance described what he called forged ancient manuscripts, naming the papal secretary Poggio Bracciolini and a bounty paid for old texts, while the host recalled museum curators who could not trace their documents. The host later argued that modernity broke reality into artificial parts and that much science relied on models. Chance relayed claims from Mark Gober's book that no virus had been isolated or shown to cause illness, and described worldview warfare as the real struggle. These were their views and were not independently verified."}, {"title": "How Remote Biofield Sessions Worked", "body": "The host asked how tuning worked over Zoom, and Chance explained that he used a table and a surrogate body built from crystals and candles matched in color and symbolism to the energy centers. He said he believed remote work was more effective for him, and that a loud music festival, where he could not hear the forks, convinced him distance was no obstacle. Chance said he made no promises or guarantees, described the work as collaborative pattern recognition with the client, and said nearly half of his sessions were repeat clients."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined John Coleman of the Apocatastasis Institute to talk about biofield tuning, and why I believe the body lives in the mind and not the other way around.
